dedupe_keys.name: global database of historic and real time flood events from social media global flood monitor

description: This database lists flood events detected from Twitter posts worldwide, where an event is flooding in a country or first-order administrative subdivision. The method, developed on 88 million tweets in 11 languages, derived more than 10,000 flood events across 176 countries in just over four years; with strict parameters about 90 percent of detected events were validated as correct, and in countries whose first official language is covered it detected 63 percent of the events in the NatCatSERVICE database at admin 1 level, as well as many events that database missed. It was published by Jens de Bruijn, Hans de Moel, Brenden Jongman, Marleen de Ruiter, Jurjen Wagemaker and Jeroen Aerts at the Institute for Environmental Studies of VU Amsterdam, in Scientific Data (2019), with results shown on the Global Flood Monitor site. Version 2.0 of 14 May 2019 is accessible on Zenodo as three free CSV files (strict, balanced and sensitive settings, 5.5 MB) under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: coverage follows Twitter use and the 11 languages, events have admin-level, not exact footprints, and the real-time stream depends on social media access that has since changed. It supports flood event catalogues for hazard exposure and emergency response studies of infrastructure; related records are EM-DAT and GDACS.
